 Brock Bowers exited the Raiders’ Week 10 game with an ankle injury. 
 A player rolled on Bowers’ ankle in a first quarter rushing play and after a trip to the blue medical tent, Bowers was helped to the locker room in the second quarter. The oft-injured Bowers seems unlikely to return. He would end his day with one catch for six yards, possibly looking at yet another injury stint. 
 -  Denny Carter

 Brock Bowers (ankle) has been ruled out in Week 10 against the Seahawks. 
 A player rolled on Bowers’ ankle in the first quarter and after a trip to the blue medical tent, he was not able to return to action. The injury-marred Bowers could be in for yet another absence, making Michael Mayer a viable fantasy option in most formats. Bowers had one catch for six yards before he suffered the ankle injury. 
 Brock Bowers 
 LV 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Brock Bowers caught 7-of-8 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers. 
 Bowers led the Raiders in routes and tied Tre Tucker for the team lead with eight targets. Though Bowers had the ball punched out on a first half reception, he played well against a stingy San Francisco coverage unit that regularly shifted coverage his way. This marked the fifth time in 2026 Bowers has exceeded 80 receiving yards, and the sixth time he’s had at least six receptions in the game. It’s incredible production for a tight end — exactly what Bowers drafters expected when they took him in August drafts. He’ll take on the Seahawks in Week 10. 
 Brock Bowers 
 LV 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Brock Bowers caught 7-of-10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets. 
 The multi-score start was Bowers’ first of the season but third of his career. He won a first quarter end zone hand fight for a 12-yarder before later contributing a two-yarder where he broke some tackles. He is now up to five touchdowns in six games and has yet to finish below 70 yards. That is league-winning type stuff out of the tight end position. The 49ers are on deck as a tough matchup up the seam for Week 9. 
 Brock Bowers 
 LV 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Brock Bowers caught 6-of-8 targets for 73 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss against the Rams. 
 Bowers seemed to be battling some sort of minor injury for most of the game, missing a few high leverage plays while staying loose on the sideline. Bowers was second on the team in targets behind Tre Tucker (12), who did most of his damage in garbage time. Bowers, who has at least nine targets in every game this season, has as high a weekly floor as any tight end in recent memory. Hopefully he’ll be able to explore some of his upside in Week 8 against the Jets.

 #89 
 Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report. 
 A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

 #89 
 Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) practiced in full on Wednesday.
 Phew. Seeing Bowers return to full participation today is heartening. The star tight end appeared on the injury report as a limited participant yesterday, leaving some questions as to when the injuries occured, and how severe they are. Ideall, he remains full tomorrow and can be started as an elite TE1 as usual against the Rams this week.

 Tight End 
 #89 
 Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice. 
 Bowers is usually a limited practice participant due to his knee injury, before upgrading to full and eventually playing. However, this week is notable as he was listed with hamstring and calf injuries instead of a knee injury. He was still limited as usual on Wednesday but the new designations are something to keep an eye on throughout the week. 
 Brock Bowers 
 LV 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Brock Bowers caught 4-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.i 
 After being held without so much as a target in the first half of Sunday’s loss, Bowers still managed to finish the day with 70 receiving yards on a team-high nine targets. The Bills effectively shadowed Bowers with cornerback Christian Benford for much of the game but Bowers took advantage of a few holes in the Bills’ zone defense to make a few plays, which included back-to-back catches of 18 and 29 yards in the fourth quarter. Bowers did in one half what most tight ends need a full game to do, which speaks to his ability as one of the top play-making tight ends in the league. He’ll remain on the TE1 radar next week against the Rams.

 Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills. 
 One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

 The Raiders continue managing Bowers’ practice reps early in the week, though he plays unrestrictedly on game day. The Raiders face the Bills in Week 6, likely facilitating a fantasy-friendly game environment. Bowers should be treated as the overall TE1 as usual this week.

 Tony Pollard rushed nine times for 33 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars, adding eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown.
 Pollard was bottled up on the ground throughout this contest, but Cam Ward leaned on him for easy completions as the Titans played from behind. Pollard eventually cashed in on one of them with a 32-yard score on a simple check-dowk. Pollard broke several tackle attempts from Jagaurs defenders that could only be descried as effortless. The return of Tyjae Spear had no impact on his role, though that could change as Spears gets healthier. Pollard remains a volume-based RB2 for his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Xavier Worthy was held without a reception on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons. 
 With Josh Downs making his Chiefs debut, Patrick Mahomes had his best game since 2022. Worthy, sadly, could not get in on the fun, turning in his first 2026 “zero ball” while only really popping up during the broadcast when he failed to corral a fourth quarter onside kick attempt. Worthy was playing through a hamstring injury, but he did not look much worse for the wear. Today was sad confirmation that what little WR4 value Worthy had left is probably now gone with Downs’ arrival. That includes even for plus dates like next week’s contest with the Cardinals. 
 -  Patrick Daugherty

 Cowboys S DaRon Bland (ankle) will not return in Week 10’s game against the 49ers.
 Bland could be seen having his right ankle tended to on the sideline in the second quarter of Sunday’s game. The 27-year-old corner was ruled out at the beginning of the second half and entered the game with an ankle injury that had him listed as questionable entering the weekend. Hopefully this isn’t an issue that plagues him for too long, as Dallas can ill-afford to lose its top defenders.

 Belinger caught a goal line touchdown in the second quarter. It was his first touchdown as a Titan. It was also the first receiving touchdown for any Titans tight end this year. Bellinger isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 11, but his presence should preent fantasy managers from having interest in Gunnar Helm.

 George Holani (knee) has been ruled out in Week 10. 
 Holani picked up the knee injury in the first half against the Raiders and did not return. The Seattle rushing offense has revolved around Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price in recent weeks, leaving Holani out of the backfield fold. He can remain on waivers ahead of Week 11.

 Kyle Pitts caught 4-of-5 targets for 50 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs. 
 The four catches were Pitts’ most in three weeks, while the 50 yards were his second most of the season. Unfortunately, that latter stat tells you all you need to know about Pitts’ TE1 viability right now — he doesn’t have any. He’s also now been held scoreless in 7-of-10 appearances. Headed on bye before returning against the Vikings’ shutdown defense, Pitts is a drop candidate in 12-team leagues.

 Tyler Shough completed 25-of-35 attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panther, adding six rushes for 25 yards. 
 Shough continued his wildly inefficient ways. He faced constant pressure from a Carolina front seven that entered the week with the league’s sixth lowest QB pressure rate, and missed short and intermediate throws throughout. Shough had a miserable aDOT of 4.5 and had a -8 total EPA on the day. The disjointed Saints offense doesn’t make things easy for Shough, but his total inability to make routine throws is having a real impact on Saints pass catchers. Shough should be considered a superflex-only option in Week 11 against the Bears. 
 -  Denny Carter

 Chimere Dike caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
 Coming off a 5-71-1 receiving line versus the Bengals, Dike appeared to be taking on a larger role in the absence of Carnell Tate. That wasn’t the case versus Jacksonville and he finished fifth on the team in targets. Even desperate fantasy managers can send him back to the waiver wire ahead of Week 11.

 Gunnar Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars. 
 Helm is up to 16 catches over his past four games, but he’s still looking for his first touchdown of the year. Daniel Bellinger stole a short score in this game. Helm also has just one game over 30 yards to his name. He’s developed a modest PPR floor, but there’s no ceiling to be had headed into his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

 Kevin Coleman caught 1-of-6 targets for six yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
 Coleman was second on the Dolphins with six targets on the day, though he caught just one for six yards. He also drew a key defensive pass interference against Sauce Gardner in the second quarter. With Chris Bell (knee) out, Coleman was No. 3 in wide receiver snaps for the Dolphins. He can be rostered in 14-team leagues as a desperation boom-or-bust play for Week 11 against the Bills.
